text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar begins a two-day visit to Germany on Wednesday. He is scheduled to meet representatives of Deutsche Bank and top officials of the federal states of Hessen and Baden-Wurtenttemberg.

- Steel maker VSZ is interested in acquiring 19 percent stakes in the two largest Czech steel producers Vitkovice and Nova Hut. VSZ's final goal is the creation of a strong group of central European steel producers and their subsequent integration.

- The National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) said there was no reason to expect a devaluation of the Slovak crown because of the worsening trade balance and balance of payments, saying hard currency reserves covered more than 3.5 months worth of imports.
- The finance ministry has said individual and corporate taxes should not increase in the near future.
HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Slovak enterpreneurs have critised the recently approved amendment to the law on bankruptcies, preventing state-run and strategic companies from going into liquidation
- The NBS has warned that if the negative trend in Slovakia's imports continues it could have a negative impact on the quality and competitivenes of the country's production.

- The development programme of Slovakia's chemical and pharmaceutical industry will require investments of around 60 billion crowns by the year 2000. About half of the sum will be covered by the industry's own resources.
- VSZ has been chosen to act as an intermediary for the exchange of information and contacts between steel producers in eastern and central Europe.
PRAVDA - On Friday, Ekoagrobanka should inform its clients on the date for the re-openning its Slovak network.
SME - The Finance Ministry has approved an increase in maximum prices of petrol fuels, the fourth such move this year, at the request of the country's sole oil refiner Slovnaft.
- Deputy Finance Minister Jozef Magula, has offered his resignation.
